scope: One-electron spinless point-Coulomb Friedrichs Hamiltonian; kappa2>kappa1>0, each fixed finite R>0; lowest m=0 and lowest |m|=1 bright sector states; unboosted nuclear charge-center Ly.

five_links.rationale: Each fixed-m meridional Friedrichs sector has negative discrete ground spectrum from its attractive Coulomb tail. Positivity improvement on connected rho>0 gives a strictly positive simple ground. The m=+/-1 degeneracy is azimuthal and not a second meridional ground. The lowest-sector branches bind the stipulated 1s_sigma and UA 2p_pi continuation; no assertion applies to excited nodal pi.

Dirichlet restriction raises the form infimum. Equality at negative E_m would be an attained half-space discrete eigenvalue because the essential threshold is 0; its zero extension belongs to the full form domain and minimizes the full quotient, contradicting the positive full ground. Hence lambda_m_plus>E_m. Reflection preserves radial kinetic and centrifugal terms. For w=u_plus-u_minus the right side is (V_minus-V_plus)u_minus>0. Its plane trace is 0; reflected functions preserve the same physical axis condition. Testing with the negative part gives minus the coercive shifted form on the left and a nonnegative dual pairing on the right, forcing no negative part. The strong maximum principle in rho>0 then makes the order strict. Potential multiplication is well-defined as a form dual pairing by Coulomb form bounds.

zeta=z+delta is a coordinate translation only, retaining (zeta-delta)dx and the -delta p_x lever term. Charge balance kappa1*z1=-C_R and kappa2*z2=C_R produces the paired torque kernel. Each factor of the paired Q6 integrand is strictly positive for rho,zeta>0; absolute convergence permits pairing. Thus the integral of the specified exact eigenstates, not only the operator, is positive.

The m=1 form embeds in the m=0 form. Removing its centrifugal term gives E0 <= E1-t integral(|A|^2/rho^2)<E1, with a finite strictly positive integral by the physical m=1 form condition. Coulomb Hamiltonians have H2 eigenfunction regularity; negative bound-state exponential decay includes local elliptic control of weighted first and second derivatives. Consequently finite-origin Lpsi exists and is in H1 form domain: near each cusp its first derivative may have 1/d singularities, which are square integrable in 3D. No Lpsi in D(H) is needed or inferred. Hardy bounds control the absolute torque product, while cusp regularity and infinity decay remove excision/cutoff terms. The quadratic-form eigenstate commutator is justified, yielding (E0-E1)L=i*hbar*C_R*T_R and hence the negative-imaginary nonzero expression.

Equal charges give reflection-even ground functions and zero paired torque. Dark pi is odd in y and is excluded by reflection. R=0 has central-l selection; no leading small-R power is inferred. Excited pi need not obey ground-state reflection order. Bare fixed-origin overlap is not an ETF-completed or origin-invariant physical amplitude, a finite effect estimate, support selector or discrepancy explanation.

clarifications_not_missing_assumptions: Weighted derivative decay and Lpsi in H1 are standard consequences of the stated fixed finite-R point-Coulomb bound eigenstate setting; explain this implication rather than claim Lpsi in D(H).
The negative-part test uses the nonnegative Coulomb form-dual pairing, not an unjustified globally smooth or L2 right side.
The sector labels are the explicit lowest-state refinement in CONVENTION_BINDING, not a result for every state carrying a pi or shell label.
